gholam.text:
رفقا، بیل گیتس یه یادداشت مفصل شیش‌هزار کلمه‌ای منتشر کرده و هشدار داده که ورود به عصر هوش مصنوعی قراره یکی از پردردسرترین دوران‌های تاریخ بشر باشه و موج بزرگی از بیکاری دائمی راه بندازه. حرف حسابش اینه که هوش مصنوعی خیلی سریع‌تر از انقلاب‌های فناورانه قبلی جلو می‌ره و مستقیم جای فکر کردن انسان رو می‌گیره؛ از برنامه‌نویسی و کارهای حقوقی گرفته تا امور مالی و پزشکی، تازه تا قبل از سال ۲۰۳۰ ربات‌ها هم به کارای ساختمونی و خدماتی هجوم میارن. گیتس حتی پیشنهاد داده برای مهار این وضعیت، روی توکن‌های هوش مصنوعی و ربات‌ها مالیات سنگین ببندن و یه‌سری مشاغل رو رسماً به عنوان «فقط برای انسان» قفل کنن تا آدما کاملاً از چرخه کار حذف نشن.

اهمیتش اینه که وقتی یکی از پدرخوانده‌های دنیای فناوری اعتراف می‌کنه این فناوری می‌تونه نسل بعدی مشاغل رو برای همیشه نابود کنه، یعنی امنیت شغلی همه‌مون وارد یه فاز فوق‌العاده حساس شده.

links.text:
Bill Gates just warned AI could trigger mass unemployment

In a super long (6,000-word) post that @BillGates just published, he says 

"Even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history"

Some takeawys 

- AI is moving too fast for the usual technology-transition playbook. Unlike PCs, AI already runs on devices people own, communicates in natural language, and can learn from the same materials used to train humans, so adoption does not require decades of new hardware, software, and user retraining. 

- He would probably support a credible global effort to slow AI development, but does not believe geopolitical and economic competition will allow one.

- His biggest economic fear is permanent job destruction, not temporary unemployment. Gates argues that AI can substitute directly for human cognition, putting entry- and mid-level work in sales, customer support, software engineering, paralegal work, finance, healthcare and other fields at risk, while increasingly capable robots could start competing for construction and hospitality tasks before 2030. 

- The decisive point comes when AI becomes reliable enough to work without human checking, because removing the human then becomes economically attractive.

- He sees AI as a force multiplier for both attackers and powerful institutions. Lower-skill criminals could gain capabilities for cyberattacks, fraud, deepfakes and potentially biological threats, while governments could use cheaper autonomous weapons, surveillance and opinion manipulation; beyond misuse by humans, 

- Gates also leaves open the longer-term risk that increasingly capable AI systems could act against human interests.

-  He worries that always-available, agreeable AI companions could reduce the difficult social interactions through which children build resilience, while heavy reliance on AI for intellectual work could weaken critical thinking; at the same time, he argues that carefully designed AI tutors could improve education by preserving the student's own cognitive effort instead of simply supplying answers.

-  He also proposes a "Human Reserved" category for work society deliberately keeps human, and taxes on AI tokens and robots to slow some automation.
